# `scc_export` — version 1.1

Source: `presets/scc/scc-export.satz`

## Purpose

Security Command Center findings, exported to BigQuery as they are raised —
where findings are KEPT, as opposed to where they are sent.

A notification tells somebody now; an export answers "what did this
organisation look like in March". Both read the same findings, and an estate
usually wants both: `presets/scc/scc-notifications.satz` is the other half.

FOUR RESOURCES, AND THE ORDER MATTERS. The dataset's project needs the BigQuery
API, so the pack enables it and takes the dataset's project THROUGH that
resource — otherwise the two race on a first apply and the dataset loses.
Even then the first apply can fail with "The project … has not enabled
BigQuery": the API is on, and BigQuery's own control plane is a minute behind.
Run the apply again; it is the same estate either way.

The exporting identity is
`service-org-<organisation>@gcp-sa-scc-notification.iam.gserviceaccount.com` —
the same agent that publishes notifications, and the `principal` the export
reports. Security Command Center grants it WRITER on the dataset itself when
the export is created; the estate declares the grant anyway, because an access
the estate depends on belongs in the estate, and a non-authoritative
`_iam_member` converges with what Google wrote.

The dataset's location is a data-residency decision and cannot be changed
afterwards. Where the CIS pack enforces `gcp.resourceLocations`, a location
outside the allowed list is refused at apply — the default follows the estate's
own default region, which that list already permits.

CHANGING ONE AFTERWARDS. The export's own fields do not update in place: the
provider sends `name` with the update and the API refuses it. A new description,
dataset or filter is applied by replacing the export —
`satz apply -replace=google_scc_v2_organization_scc_big_query_export.<label>` —
which keeps the dataset and everything already in it.

NO CLAIM. No catalog control covers Security Command Center, so this pack
witnesses nothing.

## Use it

```
params {
  // the pack's own defaults — copy only the lines you change
  scc_export_project = infra_project_name
  scc_export_dataset_id = "{customer_shortname}_scc_findings"
  scc_export_location = default_region
  scc_export_id = "satz-findings"
  scc_export_description = "Security Command Center findings, exported continuously"
  scc_export_filter = "state="ACTIVE""
}

use "presets/scc/scc-export.satz"
```

**Needs from outside the pack:**

- `customer_organization_id` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `customer_shortname` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `default_region` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `infra_project_name` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.

## Questions

What to ask before this pack is configured, and what changing the answer costs.

| asks about | prompt | reversal | blast | recommends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scc_export_project` | The project that holds the BigQuery dataset of findings | recreate | high | — |
| `scc_export_location` | Where the findings dataset lives (a BigQuery location, e.g. europe-west3 or EU) | recreate | high | — |

**scc_export_project** — Whoever can read the dataset can read every finding the organisation has ever raised, including the ones still unfixed. It is also where the BigQuery bill lands.


**scc_export_location** — A dataset's location cannot change: moving it means a new dataset and copying the history. Findings describe the estate's weaknesses, so where they are stored is a data-residency decision. Where the CIS pack enforces allowed resource locations, a location outside that list is refused.

## History

| version | date | change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | 2026-09-12 | the export pins its own `name`. The server assigns it and the provider reads it back, so without it in the config every plan proposed to null it and the API refused the update ("Field name is immutable") — a permanent diff. Measured on a live organisation |
| 1.0 | 2026-09-12 | first version: findings exported to BigQuery — the API in the dataset's project, the dataset (`delete_contents_on_destroy` false, so removing the pack does not delete the history), the exporting agent's `dataEditor` on it, and the v2 export. The dataset takes its project through the service resource, so the API is enabled first; even then a first apply can fail while BigQuery's control plane catches up, and the second succeeds. Asks the project and the location; no claim |

The whole library's history: [the changelog](../README.md#changelog) in `presets/README.md`.
